# Scene historical evidence synthesis — audit only

## Coverage and citation key

This is batch 1 of 1 for `scene_rsi_v2_2__r1`: all 12 inventoried student-trajectory files, S0013–S0024, are represented by their supplied model-reviewed audit chunks. S0019, S0020 and S0022 each have two chunks; chunk-local statements that the other chunk was unavailable do not limit this batch-level synthesis. The audits report complete source observations, but the reference and rendered images are not independently visible here. Counts are file counts, including any copies, not a count of independent trials.

For compact source citations, let **P** be `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r1/fixed_h/`. Each citation below gives the original source ID, path relative to P, and original JSONL line IDs. These are source lines, not audit-report lines.

## Evidence matrix

| Source and original path relative to P | Observed attempt and outcome |
|---|---|
| **S0013**, `H0/fixed_version_test/commons_104864364/trajectory.jsonl` | Initial build failed on a pocket fillet; an executed radius reduction passed that point but failed on a missing world. A further nonempty world revision was not executed. No render (lines 3–13). |
| **S0014**, `H0/fixed_version_test/commons_31294395/trajectory.jsonl` | Missing-world failure followed by an executed world fix and selected successful render. A later, substantial revision after image review was not executed (lines 3–14). |
| **S0015**, `H0/fixed_version_test/commons_49800017/trajectory.jsonl` | Model session timed out before any visible program or build; outcome unknown (lines 1–4). |
| **S0016**, `H0/fixed_version_test/commons_92056365/trajectory.jsonl` | Missing-world failure; the executed revision initialized a world and simplified construction, but its execution timed out without an image (lines 3–10). |
| **S0017**, `H0/fixed_version_test/commons_192968130/trajectory.jsonl` | Detailed kitchen program failed on a missing world. The traceback was received, but the next model session timed out without a revision (lines 3–9). |
| **S0018**, `H0/fixed_version_test/commons_96943062/trajectory.jsonl` | Model session timed out before a visible program, execution or render (lines 1–4). |
| **S0019**, `r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_104864364/trajectory.jsonl` | Two builds rendered and were selected. After the first render, the student diagnosed and revised furniture, stage, materials and floor selection; final response was `DONE` (lines 3–15). |
| **S0020**, `r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_31294395/trajectory.jsonl` | Two builds rendered and were selected; the student revised bed, chair, camera and lighting after review, then returned `DONE` (lines 3–15). |
| **S0021**, `r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_49800017/trajectory.jsonl` | Model invocation exited with code 1 before a visible program; stderr contents and cause are unavailable (lines 1–4). |
| **S0022**, `r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_92056365/trajectory.jsonl` | Two builds rendered; the second was selected after a student-directed framing, furniture and lighting revision. Final response was `DONE` (lines 3–15). |
| **S0023**, `r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_192968130/trajectory.jsonl` | Two builds rendered; the selected second build changed camera, cabinetry, sink and lighting after student review. The student returned `DONE` (lines 3–15). |
| **S0024**, `r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_96943062/trajectory.jsonl` | Model invocation exited with code 1 before a visible program; stderr contents and cause are unavailable (lines 1–4). |

## Comparative findings

**Technical completion is not reconstruction acceptance.** Five files show at least one successful build and render: S0014 and S0019–S0023. S0014 selected its second execution after a runtime repair, but its later image-informed revision was untested (S0014, lines 8–14). In S0019–S0023, two executions succeeded and the students returned `DONE` after the second render was supplied for review. `DONE` and selection establish completion behavior, not an independent visual score or proof that a scene matched its reference. Formal scores and overall visual correctness are unknown.

The successful render-and-revise cases show actual algorithmic behavior: students specified separate assets, materials, cameras and lights, inspected runner-supplied renders, articulated discrepancies, and executed changed programs. For example, S0019 attributed missing tiles to generic realized mesh names and changed material selection to dimensions; S0020 changed bed orientation and camera after reporting a framing and pose mismatch (S0019, lines 7–12; S0020, lines 7–12). These diagnoses are student assessments, not independently observed defects. Whether the selectors worked or revisions improved fidelity is unverified. S0023 changed camera, geometry and lighting together, so their individual effects cannot be isolated (lines 7–12).

**Failures and interruptions have different evidential meanings.** S0013 demonstrates a partial local correction: the changed fillet progressed past the first error, but the build then failed on world initialization. Its final world fix was not tested (lines 5–13). S0016 executed a broader repair and simplification but timed out; that does not establish that the repair or optimization worked (lines 5–10). S0017 received the world traceback but produced no visible correction before timeout (lines 5–9). These contrast with S0014, where conditional world creation preceded a successful render (lines 5–10); it does not follow that the same change alone would have produced a correct scene in the other cases.

S0015 and S0018 timed out during the initial model call, while S0021 and S0024 exited with code 1 and unavailable stderr. None produced a visible scene program. They are invocation interruptions, not demonstrated reconstruction-algorithm failures, partially correct scenes or empty patches. No permission or branch stop is evidenced in these files; tools being disabled in a read-only session is an access condition, not itself a permission denial. The code-1 exits are CLI/process stops of unknown cause, not evidence of a specific permission failure (S0015 and S0018, lines 2–4; S0021 and S0024, lines 2–4).

## Guidance, adoption and uncertainty

These are student trajectories, not teacher-role records. No separate teacher message, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in the group; consequently, teacher advice availability, actual receipt and adoption cannot be established. Task-system instructions and runner feedback must not be relabeled as teacher advice. Actual runner-feedback receipt is evidenced, for example, by S0014’s traceback in line 6 and its subsequent executed world initialization in lines 8–10; the successful render validates execution, not visual quality. S0019–S0023 received renders for comparison and made student-authored revisions; their reported diagnoses and actual edits are distinguishable from independently verified improvement. Session logs reporting zero tool calls do not negate the separately recorded runner executions.

Across the successful and failed scene programs, named child parts, object coordinates, procedural materials, poses, camera and lighting settings show intended construction, not verified physical connections, reference correspondence or image quality. The classroom, bedroom, cafeteria and kitchen labels are student interpretations of images unavailable to this audit. Occluded geometry, object coverage, texture appearance, framing, illumination and artifacts therefore remain unresolved. In particular, the particular floor-name, furniture-placement and camera hypotheses are task-specific; they should not be generalized into fixed corrections.

The transferable constraint is evidential: distinguish a runnable scene, feedback receipt, executed revision, selection or `DONE` from independently observed visual fidelity. Runtime initialization and execution budgets matter in these records, but the mix of completed renders, failures and interrupted calls does not establish causal superiority of either condition. No old model cost can be recovered from absent usage records, and no missing formal score should be treated as a failure or success. This synthesis is audit-only and supplies no new solution, skill or Test feedback.
